name: The Minoan-Mycenaean background of Greek civilization
plain_explanation: Before classical Greece, an artistically brilliant maritime civilization existed in Crete (Minoan) and passed to the Greek mainland (Mycenaean); successive waves of Greek-speaking invaders (Ionians, Achaeans, Dorians) eventually destroyed it, leaving only legends and archaeological remains.
precise_definition: The archaeologically reconstructed sequence running from Cretan Minoan civilization (c. 2500-1400 B.C.), through its spread to and degeneration on the Greek mainland as Mycenaean civilization (to c. 900 B.C.), ending with its destruction, largely by Dorian invaders.
why_it_mattered: Establishes the material and religious inheritance (including cults later identified with Artemis) on which historical Greek civilization, and eventually Greek philosophy, was built.
historical_origin: Reconstructed mainly through the archaeological work of Sir Arthur Evans and others, and through Egyptian and Hittite records.
examples: The palace of Minos at Knossos
The Homeric poems as a legendary memory of the Mycenaean age
connection_to_politics_or_religion: The Cretan 'Mistress of Animals' goddess cult is presented as an ancestor of the classical Artemis.
